short: A restrictive Athenian law pushed by Pericles that limited citizenship solely to those whose parents were both Athenian citizens.
full:
Prior to this law, aristocratic Athenians frequently intermarried with elites from other Greek cities to cement diplomatic and political alliances. Pericles' legislation abruptly ended this practice by decreeing that full citizenship rights—and the state benefits that accompanied them, such as jury pay and political participation—required both an Athenian father and an Athenian mother.

The law reinforced the exclusivity of the Athenian citizen body at a time when the city's imperial wealth was growing rapidly. It sharply differentiated citizens from metics (resident aliens) and fostered a stronger sense of shared identity and democratic equality among Athenians, though it severely restricted social mobility for foreigners.
